No one said it was a gambling establishment. But these boxes are very much a gamble mechanic. This game isn't alone in it; in fact, most freemium games have gamble mechanics like this one. Some countries even have laws where mechanics like this have to show the percentage of obtaining a specific item due to gambling. Sadly, in North America, we don't have such regulations, so we are left in the dark.

For the record, I don't think there's a single person that disagrees with what your post was about. And I personally do not support this type of mechanics. Do I think my choice not to purchase these boxes sends a message? Sure. Do I think anything will change? No. Why? Because this type of game attracts high spenders who go all in on things like this.

The whole point of my post was to explain to you what the boxes are. They aren't meant to provide a discount for your money, i.e., only items worth a certain number of shards or more.

They are meant to raise the ceiling of their maximum profits. Going by your scenario, if they had ten items at a maximum of a certain value with no filler, then people would either buy all for that amount or enough until they get what they want. That said, it has the side effect of very clearly becoming a "pay-to-win" scenario, and on top of that, it has a ripple effect on the tuning of the event and their profits from other aspects, such as people who buy this stuff potentially not speeding up progress anymore or not spending shards on other items.

By doing it the way they are doing, they seek to achieve a higher "average" profit due to people spending more money than they would otherwise.

It might sound very dramatic, but this is indeed gambling, and it's a psychological trap to get you to think you "win" when you get items that would be worth more than a certain number of shards and have another go. Eventually, even if you bought all boxes to get what you wanted, you end up with a feeling of "Oh well, at least I'm set for this item and this item, and I can use this item to buy this thing, and I didn't want this trinket, but at least the collection is complete. And hey, I got my costume!"
